_note_field: MAINTAINER-ONLY. `note` records why a card is modelled the way it is -- provenance, schema reasoning, what was deliberately not modelled. Never render it in the UI. `caution` is the user-facing field.
_common_note: `common` is a POPULARITY RANK, 1 to 20, and it is EDITORIAL. There is no public card-level ranking of US cardholders -- Nilson publishes issuer volume, not how many people hold a Freedom Unlimited -- so this is judgement, not a sourced fact, and it is the only field here that is. It orders the setup picker so a new user meets mass-market cards first. Re-rank it freely; nothing computes from it.
_comment: All 20 records verified against issuer sources; 7 on 2026-08-29, 7 on 2026-09-09 and 6 on 2026-09-10. Each carries its source_url. Chase Freedom Flex rotating categories MUST be re-verified 2026-10-01. Amex Platinum is deliberately absent: its 5X flight and prepaid-hotel rates are published, but no reachable americanexpress.com page stated the annual fee or the base rate on 2026-09-10, and a card modelled without those two numbers ranks wrong.

bofa-customized-cash.note: Kept because people hold it, not because it exercises the schema. Its 3% is ONE category the cardholder picks from eleven, which is what selection_group is for: without it the only choices are giving all eleven 3% (overstates badly) or picking for the user (worse). tier_multiplier is the Preferred Rewards relationship bonus and is the difference between 3% and 5.25%, so dropping it would understate the card by up to 75%.
